Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer whose printer chat has an AI that helps people add and connect printers. Between 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-04 Kenneth ran live chats connecting his Bambu P1S, a Moonraker in Docker, and his Raspberry Pi Klipper printer, and the AI repeatedly told people something false at the moment it mattered. A session on 2026-11-04 diagnosed the Moonraker runs from the transcripts the AI saw; two of the causes were facts the app held and left out of its messages (Klipper's state after a passed test; whether a key was sent before a 401). Kenneth's standing rules from this work: the app reports what it observed and forwards the source's own words; no guessed causes and no new checks to tell causes apart; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description, the standing prompt holds principles only; changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files are to be avoided and need his approval one by one; fix nothing without reproducing it; no live-model runs without his approval of a specific batch; temporary notes stay untracked and are never hidden from git status. He wants to confirm the list before any fix. Earlier sweep history: a 2026-11-01 sweep found eleven "tool says less than the app knew" places and Kenneth kept only three, so apply his test per case and do not count code shape alone. Branch: jusprin-newui at e27c962864 or later.

Task:
Sweep the printer chat's connection code for places where the app writes a message or tool result to the AI at a moment when it holds a fact the AI needs and leaves it out. List what you find and stop for Kenneth's confirmation before fixing anything.

The two known cases, which define the shape you are looking for:

1. When a Moonraker connection test passes, `PrinterConversation::tick` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`) writes "Connection to <printer> verified." The app had Klipper's state in hand: OrcaSlicer's `Moonraker::test` (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp`, lines 60-99) reads `result.klippy_state` from Moonraker's `/server/info` reply and only logs it; the fork's `OrcaPrinterBackend::settle` keeps pass or fail plus the error text. In two live chats on 2026-11-04 the AI then told the person "you can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was shut down or in error. The proposed fix, which touches no OrcaSlicer-owned file: `PrintHost::test` is virtual and `Moonraker` keeps `make_url` and `set_auth` protected, so a small fork-owned subclass of `Moonraker` can run the same test and keep the state it reads; `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host` builds the host object itself and can construct that subclass; the state travels through the attempt into the message, for example "Connection to Voron 2.4 350 verified. Klipper reports: shutdown." Then the `connect-moonraker` skill (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-moonraker/SKILL.md`) sentence that verified "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more" says the message also carries Klipper's state and what each state means for printing, labelling anything not seen on a real host as general knowledge. Entry 21 of the 2026-11-02 tool-results sweep skipped this because it seemed to need an upstream file; it does not.

2. When a connection fails after the credential form, the message is "Connection to <printer> failed: <problem>" and never says whether the form was submitted with a credential or empty, although `PrinterConversation::connect` receives the credential string. On 2026-11-04, after an HTTP 401 with the form left empty, the AI told the person "it rejected the key".

What to sweep: `PrinterConversation.cpp` (every `post_note` and every tool result for `printer_connection_status` and `printer_connect`), `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` (`connection`, `connect_host`, `connect_printer`, `settle`, `report_failure`, `connection_failure_text`), `Printers/ConnectionEvents`, and the tool descriptions for the three connection tools in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`. For each message or result, write down what the app knows at that moment (variables in scope, fields it just read, what the host or plug-in answered) and what the text says, and mark every gap. Judge each gap by Kenneth's test, which is in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` under "A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result": a person who plausibly exists, told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call. A gap the AI's next ordinary call would close is not a problem. Do not propose new checks or new branches to tell causes apart; the fix is always to forward what the code already holds (the four rules under "How to fix a result that hides the failure" in the same guide). Keep Bambu and OctoPrint behaviour as it is unless a gap there passes the test.

Done means: an untracked note at the worktree root listing every gap found, each with (a) the code location, (b) what the app knows there and what it says, (c) the person who is stuck and what they are told, (d) the fix as a forward, and (e) whether it needs an OrcaSlicer-owned file (if so, say so and propose nothing for it). The two known cases are entries 1 and 2. Then stop and put the list to Kenneth for confirmation; fix nothing until he says which. If he confirms, for each fix show the wrong message on current code and the right one after, against the Moonraker in Docker on this Mac with Klipper stopped where that applies; the shell harness's `--print-host-check` does this without a model. No live-model run. Check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, build with `-j4`, commit only when Kenneth says so, and keep notes untracked.

# Why the Moonraker connection skill did not guide the two live Klipper runs (2026-11-04)

Diagnosis only; nothing edited. Runs: openai/gpt-5.4-mini via OpenRouter, build of jusprin-newui at e27c962864. Transcripts as the model saw them: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/{moonraker,raspberrypi}-live-chat.md`. The model's web-search results are not in the transcripts (only a "web search" marker), so what it read there is not verifiable.

## The one fact that frames everything: when the skill arrives

The skill is attached to a request only when that request carries the result of a `printer_connect` or `printer_connection_status` call (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3136-3139`), and only once `connection_skill()` knows the host type, which is set by the first connect attempt (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:483-494`). So in both runs the model answered the opening message, added the printer, offered to connect, asked for the address and made the first connect call on the standing prompt alone. The skill's first chance to speak was the reply to "credential_requested". Verified from code and from where "[connect-moonraker skill added here]" sits in both transcripts.

The skill opens with "The rules above still apply." Where the standing prompt gives an exact sentence and the skill gives a fact that contradicts it, the exact sentence won every time (failures 1 and 6 below). The standing prompt is built in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`.

## Failure by failure

### 1. "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" after the person had already said so (both runs)

What the model saw: the standing prompt's connecting rule, `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING`: "after adding, offer it once: end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly 'Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?' and then 'Choices: Connect it | Not now'". No condition on whether the person already asked. Both opening messages said "I want to connect it so I can send prints to it." The conduct rule "When the person plainly states what to do ... do it: call the tool without asking again" conflicts, and the literal "exactly" rule won 2 of 2. The skill was not yet in force.
Verified: the model's text matches the prompt's sentence character for character.
Kind of change: standing prompt, not skill. The offer needs an exception for a person who already asked, or the model needs leave to go straight to asking for the address.

### 2. "If you want, I can try that address now" after "can you just try it?" (run 1)

What the model saw, three texts pointing the same way:
- `printer_connect` description (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1631-1632`): "pass only hostType and the address the person gave, and until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this."
- Connecting rule: "ask for the address they open it with in a browser ... then call printer_connect".
- Conduct rule: "When you are guessing ... ask and wait for the person's answer before adding, changing or connecting one."
The 7125 address was the model's own guess, never "the address the person gave", so by those texts it had to ask first even though the person had said "just try it". The skill's "When they want to try again, call printer_connect again with the address to use" does not say whose address counts.
Inferred: consistent with every text the model had; its reasoning is not visible.
Kind of change: tool description and skill. An address the model derived and the person agreed to try is an address to use.

### 3. "Moonraker is there, but it rejected the key" when no key was typed (run 1)

What the model saw: "Connection to Voron 2.4 350 failed: The print host test failed: HTTP 401: {...}". The app's `connect()` has the credential string the form was submitted with (`PrinterConversation.cpp:826-833`) but the note never says whether it was empty. The skill says 401 is "the same answer for no key and for a wrong key" and "wants an API key, or a different one"; nothing told the model which branch it was in, and its own two previous replies had told the person to "type it there", so it assumed a key was typed. Those replies came from the standing rule "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form", which frames the form as something to fill; the skill's "The field can stay empty" (step 3) was in context for the first of them and did not change the wording. The form label itself says "API key (if the printer asks for one)" (`components/PrinterPanel.tsx:187`), but the model never sees the form.
Verified: the note lacks the fact. Inferred: that this is why the model picked "rejected".
Kind of change: app note after a 401 says whether a key was entered. Skill frames 401 for the common case, a person who has no key and does not know what one is.

### 4. Key URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way" (run 1)

What the model saw: its search returned Moonraker's docs, which give `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key` with no port. I checked the docs: the port really is omitted there, and 7125 is Moonraker's default. The skill, in step 2 and the "Could not parse" entry, teaches that Moonraker is on 7125 and the Mainsail page is another server, but only as a matter of which address the app needs. It never says that Moonraker's own pages, the key page included, are reached at Moonraker's address and port, the same address that had just answered 401. So the model, having established "8081 is Mainsail, 7125 is Moonraker", handed the person a port-80 URL, a third server. When Chrome could not reach it, the conduct rule "When a guess is ruled out, say so and move to the next one" fit, and the model moved on instead of checking its own URL. At the same moment it called `printer_connect` a third time with nothing changed, against the rule not to repeat a failed step; my reading is that it had no next step left.
Verified: docs omit the port; the skill has no sentence about Moonraker's own pages. Inferred: the causal link.
Kind of change: skill. One sentence that the key page is at Moonraker's address and port, and that a page not reached on a different port says nothing about the key.

### 5. "Mainsail's settings page" / "an API key or access page in Mainsail's settings", never searched (both runs)

What the model saw: skill step 3, "You have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key, so search for where their version shows it before you say, and ask what they see." The sentence presupposes Mainsail shows the key somewhere. My search found no such place: Mainsail's own "connection unauthorized" FAQ sends people to `trusted_clients` in `moonraker.conf`, and Moonraker's docs give only the `/access/api_key` page and `scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`. So the model filled the skill's premise with a guess, in run 2 without any search since the one at the start of the chat, in run 1 right after two searches that had not shown such a page. The skill handed the model a sentence that says "I don't know; find out", the model found nothing, and the premise survived.
Inferred: that no Mainsail page shows the key is from my search, not from reading Mainsail.
Kind of change: skill. State what is known instead of asking the model to find it: Mainsail and Fluidd do not show the key; the two ways to get it; and that a 401 from a printer on the same home network is most often fixed by adding this computer's network to `trusted_clients`, with no key at all. That is the labelled educated guess a stuck person needs, and the skill has nothing for it.

### 6. "It's connected now, so you can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was shut down or in error (both runs)

What the model saw: the finishing rule, "after the app says the connection is verified ... For example: It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it. You can close this chat now." Both runs reproduce the example almost verbatim. The skill's step 4 says verified "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board", but the skill defers to the rules above it, and the app's note was just "Connection to X verified." The app has the Klipper state: `Moonraker::test` reads `klippy_state` from `/server/info` and only logs it (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:90-99`); the backend turns a pass into "verified" with no detail (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:766-776`). In run 2, asked "is it ready to print right now?", the model answered correctly that it could only see that Moonraker answered, so it had understood the skill; the finishing example had already made it say the opposite.
Verified.
Kind of change: app note carries `klippy_state` (already read); finishing example stops promising sending; or the skill's fact is made a rule that outranks the example.

### 7. The "send a report" card after the second failure, although the 401 was progress (run 1)

What happened: `connection_failed()` shows the card on exactly the second failure of the chat, `++m_failed_connections != 2`, by design ("The rule is the app's, not the model's", `PrinterConversation.cpp:846-860`). It does not look at what failed. The first failure (Mainsail page) and the second (401 from Moonraker) were two different steps, the second further along.
Verified. Not a skill matter.
Kind of change: app rule. Count repeats of the same outcome, or hand the judgement to the model now that it has a skill that says which step each outcome means.

### 8. Generic Klipper kept 250 × 250 although the person said 240 × 225 (run 2)

What the model saw: in add mode the standing prompt has no word about bed size. The scope paragraph that mentions bed size ("A setting the settings tools refuse, such as its bed size, is in its printer settings on this computer") is sent only to change and connect sessions; the settings-tool rules likewise. The finding rules say "Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first." The printer list gives each entry's build volume, so the model could see the mismatch, but no tool sets bed size (`printer_add` takes catalogId and nozzle only) and no rule says what to do with a stated size. The model dropped the fact silently.
Verified from `printerInstructions.ts` (`SCOPE`, `SETTINGS` gated on `!adding`).
Kind of change: standing prompt, add mode. Say that a stated bed size is changed manually in the printer's settings after adding, so the person is told rather than ignored.

## What this says about the skill as a whole

- It cannot guide the part of the chat before the first connect call, by construction. Nothing in it reached the opening offer or the address question.
- Where it states a fact that the standing prompt contradicts with an exact sentence (connect offer, finishing line), the prompt wins. The skill's own first line tells the model so.
- Its failure table says which step each outcome means, which is right, but it stops there. For the one place both runs got stuck, a 401 with a person who has no key, it tells the model what it does not know ("You have not seen where ... show the key") and sends it to search. The search returned docs the model misapplied (port) and a premise it filled with a guess (Mainsail settings). What a stuck person needs here is three labelled guesses the skill does not contain: trusted_clients on a home network; the key page at Moonraker's own address and port; the SSH script.
- Two app notes starve it: the 401 note does not say whether a key was entered, and the verified note drops the Klipper state the test already read.

Sources for the two web checks: [Mainsail FAQ: connection unauthorized](https://docs.mainsail.xyz/faq/mainsail_errors/connection-unauthorized/), [Moonraker authorization docs](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/authorization/), [Moonraker installation docs mirror (api_key page, fetch-apikey.sh)](https://server.creatbot.com/Gitea/CreatBot/CreatBotMoonraker/raw/commit/6b45c0c1d81093e27ed1b2d1d15f9bd47d0ec3b5/docs/installation.md).
# Every time the printer chat failed to help someone connect a printer, 31 October to 4 November 2026

Short version, 4 November. Words: the **standing instructions** are what the AI reads in every printer chat. The **extra connection instructions** are added by the app the first time the person tries to connect (the code calls them "skills"); they start with "The rules above still apply", so the standing instructions win a conflict. A **message from the app** is a line the app writes into the chat for the AI, such as "Connection to X failed: HTTP 401". **LAN Only** is the Bambu setting that must be on for JusPrin to connect. The **test program** plays the person from a fixed script and cannot react.

**Run 1, 31 Oct. Kenneth's P1S, LAN Only off, the shipped app.** The app said the plug-in was installed and "the printer can be connected", with no next step, so the AI asked for an address, which is the route for other printer kinds. Asked how to find it, the AI invented menu steps, because the standing instructions demand a location for every question. The app then refused with "no printer in LAN mode is on the network" before it had listened at all, and later hid the P1S it had heard with LAN Only off. The AI repeated the same three options three times, one of them a path the chat does not have, because the standing instructions forced them.

**Run 2, 1 Nov. Same P1S, app fixed to say what it heard, Sonnet.** Outcome right. Three wrong sentences: "didn't find your P1S" seconds before it was heard, because the app's 15-second "found nothing" message read as a result and nothing said a first broadcast takes 8 to 40 s; "the search stops after 15 seconds", made from "a message after 15 seconds"; and "the printer can prepare prints", copied from the app's own words.

**Run 3, 2 Nov morning. First extra instructions, a list of one step per situation. Sonnet, slow P1S.** The line for a failure said: say the app's reason in one sentence, add no cause, tell them to compare the code. With a deliberately wrong code the AI did exactly that twice and had no new idea. With Kenneth's right code it still sent him to compare the code. The real cause, a 28-second login against a plug-in that gives up at 24, was in no message from the app, and the instructions forbade a guess. The app's word "refused" was unsupported.

**Run 4, 2 Nov evening. Rewritten instructions that explain the connection. Sonnet.** With the right code the AI reasoned well ("answered just before the attempt and then went quiet, so I can't tell whether the code was wrong"). But every failure ended in "restart the printer", because the author wrote that untested step in place of the removed one, and with a wrong code the AI never suggested checking the code. The no-printer case went from 5 of 5 to 0 of 3: the rewrite dropped "ask what the screen shows" and had nothing for the moment the app says nothing was found. The AI's notes to itself appeared in the chat. DeepSeek stated "Settings > LAN" as fact. The last two are from the author's report, not read by me.

**Run 5, 2 Nov. Web search only, no extra instructions, Sonnet, healthy P1S.** Zero searches in four chats, with nothing telling the AI to search. With no printer heard it guessed "the printer isn't in LAN mode", wrong for this app, which hears a printer either way; only the removed instructions state that. It gave the code's location as fact in one chat and as a guess in another.

**Run 6, 3 Nov. New Moonraker and OctoPrint instructions, search allowed, Sonnet, test printers in Docker, a scripted person who had the key.** Six of seven connected. The one that did not was the script ignoring a correct guess. "Nothing loaded" came from the standing instructions, which say that for any connected printer. "Mainsail's address is saved" was said before the check. The key page URL was right only because the person had typed Moonraker's port 7125; the instructions never say where Moonraker's pages live. A raw stack trace reached the person.

**Run 7, 4 Nov. Moonraker in Docker needing a key, GPT-5.4 Mini, a person who does not know what an API key is.** "Want to connect it?" after the person had asked to, ordered word for word by the standing instructions. "Please type it there" to someone with no key, from the standing instructions over the extra ones' "can stay empty". "I can try that address now" instead of trying, because the address was the AI's guess and the connect action says to use only the person's address. "It rejected the key" when none was typed, because the app's message does not say whether a key was sent. The key page URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way", because Moonraker's docs omit the port and the instructions never say Moonraker's pages share its port. "Mainsail's settings page" without searching, because the instructions assume Mainsail shows the key; it does not. The report card after a failure that was progress, because the rule only counts to two. "You can send prints straight to it" with Klipper in error, because that sentence is the standing instructions' example of how to finish.

**Run 8, 4 Nov. Kenneth's Pi, no key, Klipper shut down, GPT-5.4 Mini.** The same redundant offer, the same "Mainsail's settings page", the same "send prints straight to it" (followed, when asked, by the correct "I can't see the printer's state"), and a stated 240 × 225 bed dropped without a word, since the standing instructions say nothing about bed size while adding.

367	4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.
368	
369	Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:
370	
371	| Next step | Codes |
372	|---|---|
373	| Fix the arguments and call again | `invalid_arguments`, `unknown_tool`, `unknown_skill`; the settings codes in "Error codes" below; the printer chats' own codes |
374	| Decide again: not run, because an earlier call of the same response failed (in-app only) | `not_run` |
375	| Read the state again, then call again | `not_found` (an id that is not in the open project), `stale_workspace` (the project changed since the read the call was based on), `feature_expired` (a face, edge or hole handle from an earlier revision), `connection_lost` (MCP bridge only: the outcome is unknown) |
376	| Wait, then call again | `busy` |
377	| Do the step the message names first | `needs_step` |
378	| Ask the person | `opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable` (no open project, or no FFF printer selected) |
379	| Stop and tell the person | `refused` (OrcaSlicer does not do this here), `failed` (OrcaSlicer tried and failed), `local_save_failed`, `cancelled` |
380	
381	The adapter decides the kind, because only it knows whether OrcaSlicer was busy, refused, or failed: `WorkspaceError` has a kind for each code (`NotFound`, `StaleId`, `Busy`, `NeedsStep`, `Refused`, `Failed`, `WorkspaceUnavailable`, `InvalidArgument`, `FeatureExpired`, `StaleSettings`), and the coordinator maps each one to its code in one function. Every `stale_workspace` carries the expected and the current session and revision in its details. Protocol errors at the transport level are separate JSON-RPC errors.
382	
383	A new failure picks the code whose next step fits. Add a code only for a next step none of these describe, and add it to `ToolErrors.hpp` and to this table together. The project prompt names no codes: a code and its message explain themselves. The MCP server instructions summarize the table above for external clients.
384	
385	The settings tools return these correction details, each limited in size:
386	
387	- unknown setting: the canonical code `unknown_setting`, the original key, and a short `suggestions` list;
388	- invalid enum value: the key, a diagnostic message, and the valid values in `allowed`;
389	- value out of range: the key, a diagnostic message, and the `min`/`max` bounds. Units are available from the setting's metadata;
390	- incompatible settings: the keys that conflict, and OrcaSlicer's reason;
391	- stale call: the expected and the current session/revision, plus an instruction to read again;
392	- unavailable operation: the requested scope has no active preset or target.
393	
394	A failure that should be impossible (a broken invariant) must stay visible to diagnostics and to Sentry. Catch an error at the boundary between two layers only to recover from it, to translate a known error, or to add context that is essential.
395	
396	### A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result
397	
398	Added 2026-11-01, narrowed 2026-11-02. On 2026-10-31 a Bambu Lab P1S failed to connect through the printer chat: the person gave its address, the app had heard the printer in cloud mode, and the result said "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". The right next step, turning LAN Only on, was in the app's hands and in nobody else's. The four rules above are about the code; this one is about the person on the other side of the model:
399	
400	**A refusal or an empty result is wrong when it leaves a person stuck: told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call.**
401	
402	That is the whole test, and it is applied per case, not per code shape. A sweep on 2026-11-01 found eleven places where a result said less than the app knew. Judged by this test, three were real and were fixed; the other eight were not, and their fixes were taken out again (Kenneth, 2026-11-02: "fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem"). The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call (`slice_report` after a bare `valid: false`, a search without a scope after an empty page) is not a stuck person, and every field added for such a case is text every model reads on every call. The three that were real:
403	
404	1. **A wrong Bambu access code.** Upstream's handler erases the saved code and clears the selection; a backend that read the selection said "The selected printer changed" or "The printer is no longer available", and the person, who had mistyped the code from the printer's screen, was sent to refresh a list. `Printers/ConnectionEvents` records the plug-in's answer at the moment it arrives, and the backend reads that before it reads the selection.
405	2. **A print host that answered.** A Klipper owner who types the Mainsail port instead of Moonraker's, or picks Moonraker for an OctoPrint host, was told "Could not reach the print host. Check its address, API key and network." The host was reached and said what it was. One line of the host's own answer travels with the failure.
406	3. **A heard printer the connection does not offer.** A person retrying after a failed add, with the printer's serial already linked to the first saved entry, was told "no printer of this model is on the network" while it was being heard. Every printer the search heard is in `seen` with a `reason` (`other_model`, `linked_elsewhere`, `other_device`, `occupied`, `cloud_mode`, `account_only`), and the refusal names it.
407	
408	What they share: the fork read what OrcaSlicer's event left behind (a cleared selection, a pass-or-fail flag, a filtered list) instead of the event itself, and the fakes could not produce the failing answer, so no test ever showed the sentence a person would read. The guard for a case that passes the test is a state table: arrange each state, read the tools that report it, and assert the results differ (`tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`), with the fake taught to produce every failure the real owner can (`FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, the harness's `StandInHost` with a status and body). Where a table deliberately leaves two states reading the same, a one-line comment at that assertion says why. Kenneth's rule of 2026-10-15 stands as it was: a rare failure the app has nothing more to say about gets one generic error.
409	
410	### How to fix a result that hides the failure
411	
412	Added 2026-11-02. The fix is mechanical, and a new check is almost never part of it. Four rules, in order (Kenneth, 2026-11-02):
413	
414	1. **The source gives an error: forward it.** Pass on the `what()`, the reason string or the list the code already holds, and keep any instruction the sentence carried, such as "Do not repeat the call".
415	2. **The source gives nothing: say what the code tested or saw, and delete any guessed cause.** Do not add a check or a branch to tell causes apart. If the code does not know something, the sentence stops claiming it, and there is nothing further to investigate.
416	3. **A comment says a lower layer's message misleads the model: keep the replacement.** `generate_calibration` drops the load report on purpose, because the over-the-build-volume warning is about the test model before the generator cut it. A replacement with no such comment is not protected by this rule.
417	4. **The fix needs a file OrcaSlicer owns: skip the entry.** Kenneth approves any upstream change one by one.
418	
419	A forwarded error reaches the model, so it must not name Orca or OrcaSlicer, and `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` does not see those strings.
420	
421	False successes are the exception to rule 1, because the source reports nothing. These OrcaSlicer calls do not say when they failed, so check the outcome yourself:
422	
423	- `store_stl` always returns true. `TriangleMesh::write_binary` returns false only when the file will not open, so a full disk shows only in the file size (84 + 50 per facet).
424	- `PresetBundle::export_current_configs` lists a file whether or not it was written.
425	- `Plater::split_object` returns nothing and only shows a dialog, and the model is unchanged.
426	- `ModelObject::split` splits a multi-volume object only by volume, so one solid part with a modifier stays whole however many shells it has.

# Printer chat connection messages that leave out a fact the app holds (2026-11-04)

Untracked working note. Nothing is fixed. Swept on jusprin-newui at e27c962864: every `post_note` and every
`printer_connection_status` / `printer_connect` result in `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`; `connection`,
`connect_host`, `connect_printer`, `settle`, `report_failure` and `connection_failure_text` in
`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp`; `Printers/ConnectionEvents`; and the descriptions of `printer_connection_status`,
`printer_connect` and `issue_report_open` in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`. Each entry was judged by the test in
`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` ("A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result").
Everything below was checked by reading the code. Nothing was run.

Four entries pass the test. Entries 1 and 2 are the two cases already known. Entry 3 is new. Entry 4 is new, and I am
less sure of it than of the others.

## 1. A passed Moonraker test drops Klipper's state

- (a) Where: `PrinterConversation::tick`, around line 962, writes "Connection to <name> verified.". The status tool's
  `message` is `attempt.message`, which `OrcaPrinterBackend::settle` (line 772) leaves empty on a pass.
- (b) What the app knows: the test called `Moonraker::test` (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp` lines 60-99), which read
  `result.klippy_state` (ready, startup, shutdown, error or disconnected) from `/server/info` and only logged it.
  What it says: "verified" and nothing more.
- (c) Who is stuck: a person whose Klipper is shut down or in error, and who is told "you can send prints straight to it"
  (both live runs on 2026-11-04). Their first send fails, and nobody has told them why.
- (d) Fix, a forward: a small fork-owned subclass of `Moonraker` overrides the virtual `PrintHost::test`. It runs the same
  request using the protected `make_url` and `set_auth`, and on a pass it puts the state it read into `msg`.
  `connect_host` constructs that subclass for `moonraker` in place of `PrintHost::get_print_host`. The existing
  `detail` string carries the state to `settle`, which on a pass sets the message to "Klipper reports: <state>." The
  note then reads "Connection to Voron 2.4 350 verified. Klipper reports: shutdown." The `connect-moonraker` skill's
  sentence "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more" changes to say that the note also carries Klipper's state, and
  what each state means for printing. Anything not seen on a real host is labelled as general knowledge.
- (e) No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched. The subclass repeats about 30 lines of upstream's test; the PR has to say so.

## 2. A failed connection after the form does not say whether a key was sent

- (a) Where: `PrinterConversation::connect` (line 835) and `tick` (line 963) both write "Connection to <target> failed:
  <problem>".
- (b) What the app knows: `connect` receives the credential string from the form. `connect_host` (line 734) then decides
  which key the test sends. That is the one typed into the form; or, when the form was left empty and the address and
  host type are the ones already saved, the key saved for this printer; or no key at all. What it says: the host's
  answer only, for example "HTTP 401: {...}".
- (c) Who is stuck: on 2026-11-04 a person left the form empty and got a 401, and was told "it rejected the key". A
  person with no key, who does not know what one is, then goes looking for a mistake in a key they never typed.
- (d) Fix, a forward: `HostAttempt` records which of the three cases the test used. `connect_host`'s ternary already
  makes that choice; no new check is involved. The failure says it, for example "The print host test failed, sent with
  no API key: HTTP 401: ...". This applies to OctoPrint too, since both go through `connect_host`. Kenneth decides
  whether OctoPrint is included.
- (e) No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

## 3. A printer saved with another connection type: the type is not named, and the place given is wrong

- (a) Where: `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`, lines 485-488. Its message reaches the model through
  `printer_connection_status`, and through the failure note after the form: `connect_host` returns `info.message` at
  line 723.
- (b) What the app knows: the printer's saved `host_type`, for example `elegoolink`. What it says: "Configure this
  connection type in Printer settings. You can still prepare prints and export a file." The message does not name the
  type. It also names Printer settings, and OrcaSlicer's printer settings tab has no connection setting: `Tab.cpp` has
  no `host_type` or `print_host`. Those settings live in the physical printer dialog (`PhysicalPrinterDialog.cpp`).
- (c) Who is stuck: someone with an Elegoo Neptune 4, 4 Pro, 4 Plus or 4 Max. Those profiles ship with
  `"host_type": "elegoolink"`, and the printers run Klipper with Moonraker and Fluidd. Creality K2 (`crealityprint`),
  Prusa (`prusalink`), Duet and others are in the same position. The person says it runs Klipper, and the model calls
  `printer_connect` with `moonraker`. The form opens, the person types or skips a key, and after Submit they are sent
  to a settings tab that does not have the setting.
- (d) Fix, a forward (rule 2): name the type the app read, and stop naming a place the code never checked. For example:
  "This printer is saved with the ElegooLink connection type, which this chat does not connect. It connects Moonraker
  and OctoPrint." Whether this chat should test Moonraker for such a printer anyway is a product question, and I am not
  proposing it.
- (e) No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

## 4. A verified Bambu connection drops the nozzle mismatch (less sure)

- (a) Where: `tick`, around line 962, reads `info.nozzle_mismatch` in the same `connection()` call and writes only
  "verified".
- (b) What the app knows: whether the nozzle size the printer reports differs from the saved one
  (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` lines 600-604). The standing prompt promises "A nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is
  something to offer to fix with printer_change", but only `printer_connection_status` carries it. After "verified",
  the finishing rule ends the chat, so the model has no reason to make that call.
- (c) Who is stuck: a P1S owner who fitted a 0.6 mm nozzle and saved the printer as 0.4. They are told "connected, send
  prints", and the fix (`printer_change`) is never offered. Two things are unverified. I expect the printer's first full
  report to carry its nozzle size, but I have not seen it on a real printer. I also have not checked what the send
  dialog does on a mismatch.
- (d) Fix, a forward: when `nozzle_mismatch` is true, the verified note adds "The printer reports a <x> mm nozzle; this
  printer is saved with <y> mm." `connection()` has both values.
- (e) No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

## Considered and not listed

- The credential request does not say that a saved key or access code would be reused if the form is left empty. The
  form is in front of the person, and its label says the key is optional.
- A wrong Bambu code with an empty form: "The printer refused the access code ..." is true either way and already names
  the next step.
- The plug-in's message on a lost connection is dropped (`record_connection_event` keeps text only for failures). I have
  no evidence that the plug-in sends any text with it, and upstream ignores it too.
- "Bambu's network plug-in is installed now, so X can be connected" names no next step. The standing prompt now says to
  call `printer_connection_status`, and that call is the next step.
- A saved host reads "unknown ... live printer status is not available here" while Home's poller has reached it. The
  model's next `printer_connect` closes that gap.
- A passed test whose save then fails: the save's own error is forwarded already.
- The Bambu search notes and the `seen` reasons were covered by the 2026-11-01 sweep and are unchanged.
- The three tool descriptions state nothing that the app knows to be false. "Pass ... the address the person gave"
  (diagnosis failure 2) and the report card on the second failure are rules, not held facts, so they are outside this
  sweep.
- I could not find the full list from the 2026-11-02 sweep, so I could not check these entries against its rejected
  ones, apart from its entry 21, which is entry 1 here.

Sources for entry 3's printer facts: [SimplyPrint, Neptune 4 Pro setup](https://simplyprint.io/setup-guide/elegoo/neptune-4-pro.md),
[raspberry.tips, Moonraker on the Neptune 4](https://raspberry.tips/en/3d-druck/3d-printer-home-assistant-moonraker).

The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).
